about.metaDescription: Younghoon Kim, a frontend developer with three years across EA, NHN, and Pandora TV on game operations, ticketing, and community products, with 12 fixes merged into React Router, TanStack Query, and other open-source projects.
about.intro: I spent three years building frontends at EA, NHN, and Pandora TV for game operations, concert ticketing, and a community service. At EA and Pandora TV I was the only frontend engineer. I found and fixed problems in React Router, TanStack Query, and other open-source projects, and 12 of those fixes were merged after review by outside maintainers.

items.developerExperience: Reproduction links that drop QA and developers into the same account, tab, and position
items.reliableInterfaces: A publishing screen that makes version diff and DB generation checks a required step
items.runtimeBehavior: Problems that only show up on old devices and inside WebViews
items.openSource: Open-source fixes shipped with a reproduction and a test

ea.highlight1: Sole frontend engineer on the 20-person FC Online SE team, turning account, item, and content requests from QA and server developers into screens and verification flows
ea.highlight2: Turned the account and screen position where a bug appeared into a reproduction link. The URL owns the account, tab, and detail position and TanStack Query fetches the data, so QA lands on the same screen from one Slack link
ea.highlight3: Put version diff and per-file DB generation checks on one screen before publishing, and blocked publishing until every required generation succeeded. The same kind of bad publish has not recurred since. Rechecked accessibility on 10 routes including login with axe-core and Playwright

nhn.highlight1: One of three developers from a seven-person FE team assigned to TicketLink, owning the React 18 and TypeScript migration of the show list and detail pages plus the international user screens
nhn.highlight2: Reproduced Safari crashing on old iPhones during long list scrolls on a test device, then added TanStack Virtual so only the visible range stays in the DOM. The crash did not recur under the same procedure
nhn.highlight3: Kept filters and scroll position when returning from detail or booking to the list, and merged the international site into the Korean React codebase so Korean, English, Japanese, and Chinese screens ship from one codebase

pandora.highlight1: Sole frontend engineer for Cobak web and WebView screens: post writing and editing, membership, and public pages
pandora.highlight2: After an in-app payment, the returning WebView invalidates the related queries, reloads payment and membership state from the server, and cancels overlapping earlier requests. Pending, failed, and complete screens are covered by component tests
pandora.highlight3: Built manual save, a draft list, restore, and delete so long posts survive app exits, and split the publish and draft entry points so neither depends on client state ordering

openSource.heading: Merged open-source work
openSource.lead: Fixes in React Router, TanStack Query, and other React ecosystem projects for performance bottlenecks, runtime regressions, browser compatibility, and type problems, each reproduced first and shipped with a test. These are 10 representative PRs out of 12 merged.

query.pr1Title: Optimized useQueries from O(N²) to O(N)
query.pr1Desc: Reduced function calls in the 500-query benchmark from 4,500 to 2,000 (about -55%).
query.pr2Desc: Resolved stale UI after page refresh.
query.pr3Desc: Stabilized a mismatch in the Nx Cloud distributed execution config.

router.pr2Desc: Added safe handling for session save failures in private mode.
router.pr3Title: Fixed fetcher.submit treating plain objects as HTML elements
router.pr3Desc: Plain objects with a tagName were handled as form elements. Fixed and added a regression test.
router.pr5Desc: Fixed CSS preload failing behind a CDN with CORS.

rhf.pr1Desc: Resolved the never-lock issue and added type tests.

tsr.pr1Desc: Changed 500 to 404 behavior and added tests.

openSource.firsttx: FirstTx: five npm packages that save CSR screen state, restore it on revisit, and roll back on failure, with docs, a Playground, DevTools, and releases that I maintain. On top of it I built Bug Dreamer, a checker that generates boundary-state tests and reports only failures it can reproduce in isolation, validated against 20 pre-registered defects with 7 published reproduction reports.
openSource.mentoring: Code review mentoring: four sessions in late 2025 for about 50 students across Programmers K-Digital Training cohorts.

stack.heading: Tools I use now
stack.line: React, TypeScript, and Next.js as a base. TanStack Query, React Router, and Zustand for state and routing. Vite, Vitest, Playwright, and ESLint for build and tests. Node, Fastify, Prisma, and tRPC when I need a backend.
